Wars & Captivity

Tomb of Sultan Ahmed I (resting place of Osman II)

Here lies Sultan Osman II, who in 1621 faced Hetman Chodkiewicz at Khotyn – and who lost his throne and his life a few months after returning from that campaign.

Theme
Wars & Captivity
District
Fatih
Period
1621–1622
Visiting
Open to visitors

The story

In this tomb lies the sultan who in 1621 led his army to Khotyn against the camp of Hetman Jan Karol Chodkiewicz: young Osman II completed his father's mausoleum in 1619, and only three years later was buried in it in secret.

Osman came to the throne in 1618 at the age of about fourteen. In the summer of 1621 he led a vast army to the Dniester against the fortified camp of the Polish-Lithuanian and Cossack forces at Khotyn (Chocim). The defence was commanded by Hetman Jan Karol Chodkiewicz, who died in the besieged camp, and then by Stanisław Lubomirski.

How to visit

The tomb stands in its own walled garden on the north-eastern side of the Blue Mosque, by Sultanahmet Square. It is a place of burial and prayer: dress modestly and take your shoes off at the door. It is usually open and free, but hours can be shorter at prayer times and on religious holidays, so check on the day. Inside are 36 cenotaphs, among them those of Ahmed I, his consort Kösem, Osman II and Murad IV; look for the İznik tiles and the ebony door inlaid with mother-of-pearl and ivory.
